graphing part 2

Amanda Mae Woodward

2026-11-03

  1. Open the starwars dataset (located in tidyverse)
library(tidyverse)
## Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.4.3
## Warning: package 'tidyr' was built under R version 4.4.3
## Warning: package 'readr' was built under R version 4.4.3
## Warning: package 'purrr' was built under R version 4.4.3
## Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 4.4.3
## Warning: package 'lubridate' was built under R version 4.4.3
## ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ──
## ✔ dplyr     1.2.0     ✔ readr     2.2.0
## ✔ forcats   1.0.1     ✔ stringr   1.5.1
## ✔ ggplot2   4.0.2     ✔ tibble    3.2.1
## ✔ lubridate 1.9.5     ✔ tidyr     1.3.2
## ✔ purrr     1.2.1

data(starwars)
  1. Create a scatter plot of character’s height and mass.
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+ geom_point()
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

2a. Change the color and shape of the points in your scatter plot.

ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass))+ geom_point(color = "cadetblue", shape = 18)
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Add Homeworld as a third variable to your scatterplot.
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color = homeworld))+ geom_point(shape = 18)
## Warning: Removed 28 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

3a. What do you notice about the graph? (e.g. describe what you see)

# there is a generally positive correlation of height vs mass with a major outlier at 175, ~1750. most heights are 150-200 and masses are 0-200 ish.
  1. Make a boxplot of height.
ggplot(starwars, aes(height))+ geom_boxplot()
## Warning: Removed 6 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

  1. Make a boxplot of height for each species present in the data.
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, species))+ geom_boxplot()
## Warning: Removed 6 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

5a. change the appearance of your graph in at least 3 ways.

ggplot(starwars, aes(height/100, color = species))+ geom_boxplot() + labs(x = "Height (m)", y = "Weight (kg)") + theme_minimal()
## Warning: Removed 6 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).

  1. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from viridis.
library(viridis)
## Loading required package: viridisLite
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color = species)) + geom_point()+ scale_color_viridis(option = "mako", discrete = TRUE)
## Warning: Removed 31 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

7.Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph that uses a color palette from RColorBrewer.

ggplot(starwars, aes(height, mass, color = gender)) + geom_point() + scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1")
## Warning: Removed 31 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

  1. Using any variables in the starwars dataset, create a graph using facet_wrap
ggplot(starwars, aes(height/100, color = species))+ geom_boxplot() + labs(x = "Height (m)", y = "Weight (kg)") + facet_wrap(~species)
## Warning: Removed 6 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_boxplot()`).
